editorial_contributions.text: The problem of determining the minimum number of colors that are needed to color the points of the plane so that no two points unit distance apart are assigned the same color is considered. This number is referred to as the chromatic number of the plane denoted by \(\chi(\mathbb{E}^2)\). One of the problems that prevailed in the literature is ``What is the smallest order of a 4-chromatic unit distance graphs of girth 4?''. In this article, the authors construct triangle-free 4-chromatic unit distance graphs with 21, 19, and 17 vertices. The authors present an evidence that the value 17 cannot be improved.

editorial_contributions.text: Paul Erdös posed the question: are there any 4-chromatic subgraphs with no short cycles in the unit distance graph in the plane, that is, the graph whose vertices are all points in the real plane and whose edges connect all pairs of points distance 1 apart? The author constructs a 40-vertex 4-chromatic subgraph with no 3-cycles.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: We present an embedding of a 61-vertex, 5-chromatic graph of girth 4 in \(\mathbb{R}^3\) as a unit-distance graph (UDG). We speculate that no 6-chromatic case exists, even though 6-chromatic UDGs in \(\mathbb{R}^3\) with girth 3 exist having as few as 47 vertices. However, our discovery provides motivation to seek 5-chromatic cases with larger girth, not least because there exist 4-chromatic unit-distance graphs in the plane with arbitrary girth.
